bible_refs.note: Quoted with the edition's quotation marks; Cyril omits καί before ὅτι.
ἀγνοοῦντες… τὴν τοῦ Θεοῦ δικαιοσύνην / ἠγνοήκασι… τὴν ἐκ Θεοῦ δικαιοσύνην; οὐ ζητήσαντες answers Paul's ζητοῦντες στῆσαι.
Clear allusion: ἐὰν οὖν ὁ υἱὸς ὑμᾶς ἐλευθερώσῃ / τὸν υἱὸν τὸν ἐλευθεροῦν ἰσχύοντα.
Lemma Τέλος γὰρ νόμου Χριστός; restated later as τέλος… νόμου καὶ προφητῶν.
Clear allusion: ὁ νόμος παιδαγωγὸς ἡμῶν γέγονεν εἰς Χριστόν / παιδαγωγὸς ἐπὶ τὸ τοῦ Χριστοῦ μυστήριον.
Compressed: Οὐκ ἦλθον καταλῦσαι τὸν νόμον ἀλλὰ πληρῶσαι (Matthew has μὴ νομίσητε ὅτι ἦλθον καταλῦσαι τὸν νόμον ἢ τοὺς προφήτας· οὐκ ἦλθον καταλῦσαι ἀλλὰ πληρῶσαι).
Lemma, then repeated with ὁ ποιήσας ἄνθρωπος ζήσεται ἐν αὐτῇ.
Source of Romans 10:5 (LXX ἃ ποιήσας ἄνθρωπος ζήσεται ἐν αὐτοῖς).
LXX Psalm 18:13, παραπτώματα τίς συνήσει; Cyril's order Τίς γὰρ συνήσει παραπτώματα. English numbering 19:12.

pass_a_gloss: [Θεόν completes ὡς φύσει from u09-rem early] God, but they said (hoi de elegon) that: Concerning a good work (kalou ergou) we do not stone (lithazomen) you, but concerning blasphemy (blasphemias), because you being a man (anthropos) make yourself God. Or thus (e houtos). They have been ignorant of (egnoekasi) the righteousness (dikaiosynen) from God, that is, Christ, or (etoi) the [righteousness] through the faith toward him. And thinking to fight shield to shield (synaspizein) with the law through Moses, they have remained (memenekasin) disobedient (apeitheis); not having sought (zetesantes) the Son (hyion) the one able (ischyonta) to free (eleutheroun), the one justifying (dikaiounta) the ungodly (asebe), and economically (oikonomikos) contracting (systellonta) the hard to accomplish (dyskatorthoton) righteousness of the law, that he might release (apallaxe) from difficulty (dyschereias) and wearing toil (tribes). [lemma Romans 10:4] For end (telos) of law Christ. Was brought in beforehand (proeiskekomistai) therefore the law, going to be for the ancients (archaiois) tutor (paidagogos) to the mystery (mysterion) of Christ, and through riddles (ainigmaton) showing dimly (hypophainon) to them the truth (aletheian). For thus we define (diorizometha) Christ to be fulfilment (pleroma) of law and prophets, and very rightly. Or would not the true reasonably be understood to be fulfilment of every obscure (asaphous) riddle? and yet how would anyone doubt (endoiaseie)? Therefore [read οὔκουν, 'not then'] the passing over (metaphoitesis) of the things in shadows (skiais) toward the truth makes abolition (anairesin) of the laws through Moses, but establishes (kathistesi) their meaning (dianoian) more manifest (ekphanesteran). The matters having flowed over (meterrhyekoton) henceforth into truth, and the things in types (typois) and riddles having received the change (metabolen) toward the better, we say the law not to have been dissolved (katalelysthai), but rather to have been brought to completion (ekpeperanthai) at the time (kairou) in which the truth shone upon (epelampsen) us, that is, Christ. For end of law and prophets the Christ, who would not speak falsely (diapseusaito) saying: I came not to dissolve (katalysai) the law but to fulfil (plerosai). For as the many formedness (polyeides) of the colours (chromaton) brought on (prosenenegmenon) in time least of all removes (anairei) the shadows (skias) pre outlined (proanatypoumenas) in the panels (pinaxi), but rather transfers (methistesi) to a clearer (enargesteran) sight (opsin), in the equal manner to this, we say the shadows of the law not to have been overturned (anatetraphthai), but rather to have been completed as in the advance (proodo) toward truth. [lemma Romans 10:5] For Moses writes the righteousness from the law etc. For Moses writes the righteousness from the law, he says: the man (anthropos) having done (poiesas) will live (zesetai) in it; but there was no one at all able blamelessly (amometos) to accomplish (katorthosai) it; For who will understand (synesei) transgressions (paraptomata)? Therefore better (ameinon) the justifying grace (dikaiousa charis) and releasing (apallattousa) us from the indictment (graphes) in law. [lemma Romans 10:6] But the righteousness from faith speaks thus. He defines (horizetai) usefully also how the faith would come about from us, if it would have the blameless (to amometon) with God and the to seem to have been done very well; for to doubt (endoiazein) at all and to love (philein) to be shaken (katadoneisthai) into ineffectual (adrane) double mindedness (dipsychian), to be cast away (apobleton) altogether; and superfluous (peritton) perhaps and of the most dangerous (sphalerotaton) the to need (chrenai) to busy about (periergazesthai) the things also beyond all reason (logou), and are in things better than the mind (nou) according to us; for how would be manifest (emphane) the things ineffably (aporrhetos) crafted (technourgoumena) by God? and indeed what eye (ophthalmos) of heart (kardias) would be so great as to be able to behold (katathresai) God, rather who then will understand (synesei), even if someone should choose to speak and narrate (aphegoito) the things very much above us? For the (ho men gar) [continues 'our Lord Jesus Christ' in u09-rem close].
pass_b_english: …God, they said instead, “It is not for a good work that we stone you, but for blasphemy, because you, being a man, make yourself God” (John 10:33). Or it may be read in this way: they have not known the righteousness that comes from God (Romans 10:3), that is, Christ, or else the righteousness that comes through faith in him. Supposing that they were fighting side by side with the law given through Moses, they remained disobedient, not seeking the Son who is able to set free (John 8:36), who justifies the ungodly (Romans 4:5), and who, in his saving dispensation, cuts short the righteousness of the law, so hard to achieve, to give release from hardship and toil.

“For Christ is the end of the law” (Romans 10:4). The law, then, was brought in beforehand to be a tutor for the people of old, leading them to the mystery of Christ (Galatians 3:24), and to give them glimpses of the truth through riddles. That is how we define Christ as the fulfilment of the law and the prophets, and quite rightly. Or would not the truth reasonably be understood to be the fulfilment of every obscure riddle? And how could anyone doubt it? So the passage from what was in shadows to the truth does not do away with the laws given through Moses; rather, it makes their meaning clearer.

Now that things have passed over into truth, and what was in types and riddles has been changed for the better, we do not say that the law has been abolished, but rather that it has been brought to completion at the time when the truth, that is, Christ, shone upon us. For Christ is the end of the law and the prophets, and he would not speak falsely when he says, “I did not come to abolish the law but to fulfil it” (Matthew 5:17). For just as the many colours, added in due time, by no means do away with the shadowy outlines first sketched on painted panels, but rather bring them into clearer view, in the same way we say that the shadows of the law have not been overturned, but rather brought to completion, as in an advance toward the truth.

“For Moses writes of the righteousness that is from the law,” and the rest (Romans 10:5). “For Moses writes,” he says, “of the righteousness that is from the law, that the person who does it shall live by it” (Romans 10:5; Leviticus 18:5). But there was no one at all who could carry it out blamelessly; for “who will understand transgressions?” (Psalm 19:12). So the grace that justifies is better, and it frees us from the indictment that stands in the law.

“But the righteousness that is from faith speaks thus” (Romans 10:6). He usefully lays down how faith should be practised on our part, if it is to be blameless before God and to seem very well done indeed. For to doubt at all, and to be given to being tossed about into feeble double-mindedness, is utterly to be rejected; and it is perhaps superfluous, and among the most dangerous things of all, to think one must pry into what lies beyond all reason and above our understanding. For how could the things God works in ways beyond words be plain to see? And what eye of the heart could be so great as to be able to behold God? Or rather, who will understand, even if someone chose to speak and set out things that are very far above us? For…

σὺ ἄνθρω"πος ὢν ποιεῖς σεαυτὸν Θεόν·" ἢ οὕτως. ἠγνοήκασι μὲν τὴν ἐκ Θεοῦ
δικαιοσύνην, τουτέστι Χριστὸν, ἤτοι τὴν διὰ πίστεως τὴν εἰς αὐτόν. οἰόμενοι δὲ τῷ διὰ
Μωσέως συνασπίζειν νόμῳ, μεμενήκασιν ἀπειθεῖς· οὐ ζητήσαντες τὸν υἱὸν τὸν
ἐλευθεροῦν ἰσχύοντα, τὸν δικαιοῦντα τὸν ἀσεβῆ, καὶ τὴν δυσκατόρθωτον τοῦ νόμου
δικαιοσύνην οἰκονομικῶς συστέλλοντα, ἵνα δυσχερείας ἀπαλλάξῃ καὶ τριβῆς. Τέλος γὰρ
νόμου Χριστός. Προεισκεκόμισται τοίνυν ὁ νόμος, ἐσόμενος τοῖς ἀρχαίοις παιδαγωγὸς
ἐπὶ τὸ τοῦ Χριστοῦ μυστήριον, καὶ δι' αἰνιγμάτων αὐτοῖς ὑποφαίνων τὴν ἀλήθειαν.
οὕτω γὰρ εἶναι διοριζόμεθα πλήρωμα νόμου καὶ προφητῶν τὸν Χριστὸν, καὶ μάλα
ὀρθῶς. ἢ οὐχὶ παντὸς αἰνίγματος ἀσαφοῦς νοοῖτ' ἂν εἰκότως πλήρωμα ὑπάρχειν τὸ
ἀληθές; καίτοι πῶς ἂν ἐνδοιάσειέ τις; οὐκοῦν ἀναίρεσιν τῶν διὰ Μωσέως ποιεῖται
νόμων ἡ πρός γε τὸ ἀληθὲς τῶν ἐν σκιαῖς μεταφοίτησις, ἀλλ' ἐκφανεστέραν αὐτῶν
καθίστησι τὴν διάνοιαν. Μετεῤῥυηκότων λοιπὸν εἰς ἀλήθειαν τῶν πραγμάτων, καὶ τῶν
ἐν τύποις καὶ αἰνίγμασι τὴν εἰς τὰ ἀμείνω λαβόντων μεταβολὴν, οὐ καταλελύσθαι
φαμὲν τὸν νόμον, ἐκπεπεράνθαι δὲ μᾶλλον ἐπὶ καιροῦ, καθ' ὃν ἡμῖν ἐπέλαμψεν ἡ
ἀλήθεια, τουτέστι, Χριστός. τέλος γὰρ νόμου καὶ προφητῶν ὁ Χριστὸς, ὃς οὐκ ἂν
διαψεύσαιτο λέγων "Οὐκ ἦλθον καταλῦσαι "τὸν νόμον ἀλλὰ πληρῶσαι." ὥσπερ γὰρ τὰς
ἐν τοῖς πίναξι προανατυπουμένας σκιὰς, τὸ τῶν χρωμάτων πολυειδὲς ἐν καιρῷ
προσενηνεγμένον, ἥκιστα μὲν ἀναιρεῖ· μεθίστησι δὲ μᾶλλον εἰς ὄψιν ἐναργεστέραν,
κατὰ τὸν ἴσον τουτωΐ τρόπον, οὐκ ἀνατετράφθαι φαμὲν τὰς τοῦ νόμου σκιὰς,
ἐκπεπεράνθαι δὲ μᾶλλον ὡς ἐν προόδῳ τῇ πρὸς ἀλήθειαν. 236 Μωσῆς γὰρ γράφει τὴν

review_notes: Copy-text: PG 74; Fragmenta in Romanos via Khazarzar (Fragmenta in sancti Pauli epistulam ad Romanos.pdf).

Section opens mid-sentence: Θεόν completes ὡς φύσει at the close of u09-rem-early; rendered '…God' with a leading ellipsis. οἱ δὲ ἔλεγον: δέ marks the contrast with what they ought to have done, so 'they said instead'.
ἢ οὕτως: Cyril offers a second reading of Romans 10:2–3; rendered 'Or it may be read in this way'.
τουτέστι Χριστόν, ἤτοι τὴν διὰ πίστεως τὴν εἰς αὐτόν: two glosses of 'the righteousness from God'; ἤτοι rendered 'or else'.
συνασπίζειν (lit. 'to stand shield to shield with'): 'fighting side by side with'.

οἰκονομικῶς συστέλλοντα: 'in his saving dispensation, cuts short'; συστέλλω is 'contract, abridge', in line with the 'word cut short' of Romans 9:28 in u09-rem-early. ἵνα δυσχερείας ἀπαλλάξῃ καὶ τριβῆς has no stated object; rendered 'to give release from hardship and toil', nothing supplied.

οὐκοῦν ἀναίρεσιν… ποιεῖται… ἀλλ' ἐκφανεστέραν… καθίστησι: the ἀλλ' requires a negative, so read οὔκουν ('not, then'): the passage to truth does not abolish the laws but makes their meaning clearer. This matches the next sentences (οὐ καταλελύσθαι, οὐκ ἀνατετράφθαι).
ἐκπεπεράνθαι: 'brought to completion' (lit. 'carried through to the end'), Cyril's sense of τέλος here; not 'ended' in the sense of abolished.
The painter image: σκιαί are the preliminary shadow-outlines on a panel (πίναξ), later filled with colour; rendered 'shadowy outlines first sketched on painted panels'.
γραφῆς… τῆς ἐν νόμῳ: legal sense 'indictment', as in u08-rem-close; Colossians 2:14 (χειρόγραφον… τοῖς δόγμασιν) is a possible echo, not cited.
ὁ ποιήσας ἄνθρωπος: 'the person who does it', since ἄνθρωπος here is generic.

διψυχία and καταδονεῖσθαι may echo James 1:6–8 (δίψυχος, a wave tossed); possible allusion only, not cited. καρδίας ὀφθαλμός may echo Ephesians 1:18; possible only, not cited. 'Who will understand' (τίς ἄρα συνήσει) echoes the Psalm verse just quoted.
Page number 236 and the footer numeral '26' are edition apparatus and are omitted.
Section ends mid-sentence at ὁ μὲν γάρ ('For…'); u09-rem-close resumes '…our Lord Jesus Christ once set before Nicodemus…'.
